review_candidates.title: Operations Engineer II, Network
review_candidates.description: Job Description Job Type: Full-time | Location: Fort Worth, TX | Department: Innovation | Reporting to: Head of Cloud Support & Customer Engineering • Technology | Work Location: #hybrid IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC. Cloud Operations & SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) runs the IREN AI Cloud the way a hyperscaler runs theirs. Every GPU-hour we sell is available, observable, supported and billed accurately. We are growing fast as new sites come online. We do it AI-native: the assistant drafts, and a named human verifies, signs and posts. We are seeking a Technical Operations Engineer to join our Level 2 Technical Operations team in Fort Worth or Sydney. The team keeps the GPU fleet healthy 24×7: switching, routing, firewalls, backbone links, carriers and customer interconnects. You take the incidents the L1 engineers cannot close, and you own them to root cause. This is a Level 2 role on our support ladder, and it is a destination. You diagnose in your lane, you run changes to a standard, and you write down what you found. A blank handoff is not a handoff here. The step above you is Senior Technical Operations Engineer. The SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) org is our L3; it owns SLOs (service level objectives), automation and post mortems. An escalation to it carries your diagnosis. Job Requirements Two to five years in a data center, NOC (network operations center) or IOC environment, with Level 2 ownership of incidents. Core network skills at CCNA (Cisco Certified Network Associate) level or equivalent: switching, routing (BGP, OSPF), VLANs, firewalls and WAN links. Hands-on experience with Fortinet FortiGate and FortiSwitch, or transferable skills from Cisco Nexus and Firepower. You troubleshoot to root cause and write down what you checked, what you found, what you could not verify, and who acts next. Practical scripting (Python or Bash). You write and maintain a script, not only run one. Data center fundamentals: fiber optics, switches, PDUs (power distribution units), and safe work in a live hall, including electrical safety and rack-mounted equipment. Genuinely AI-native. You use AI assistants and agentic tools every day, not now and then. Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini is your daily driver, and Claude Code or an equivalent is how you build. You join systems up with Claude projects, the Atlassian and Microsoft 365 connectors, Jira Automation and Teams workflows. You can describe a workflow you automated, what broke and how you fixed it. For you, prompting is a way of working, not a party trick. Evidence before action, and that includes the assistant’s output. Every identifier in your update comes from a check you ran. A failed query reads “not found”; you never fill it in. You count from data, you never estimate, and you re-verify anything that looks too clean. Every ticket comment meets the same standard. It lists what you checked, what you found with source and time, what is not verified, and who acts next. Clear written and spoken communication: incident updates, handover notes, runbook and RCA (root cause analysis) text the next region can act on. Comfortable on a 12-hour rotating roster in a 24×7 operations center, with a structured written handover into and out of the adjacent region. Post-secondary education in computer science or engineering is an asset; equivalent hands-on experience counts the same. This role works 12-hour rotating shifts in a 24×7 operations center: 4 days on / 3 days off, then 3 days on / 4 days off. On-call participation and major incident response are part of the role. The role is office-based with periodic site visits; you travel to project locations in the US, Canada or Australia as required. Job Responsibilities The Level 2 network owner. You take the network incident the runbook cannot close and own it to root cause, in the Network and Edge lane. A diagnostician who writes it down. Every handoff carries what you checked, what you found with source and time, what is not verified, and who acts next. A comparer of neighbors. You compare the failing port, switch or firewall against its healthy sibling and attach the diff before you escalate. A safe pair of hands-on change. You execute approved network changes to a standard, with a tested rollback, and never outside the change process. An automation contributor. You retire the repeat ticket with port compares, config diffs and event-burst detection, merged with tests in IREN GitLab. An AI-native engineer. The assistant drafts your ticket evidence and handover card; you verify every line. You confirm, correct or escalate every triage-agent suggestion, and you build with Claude Code under our engineering rules. A destination, not a step. L2 is a career here, with a Senior Technical Operations Engineer above it. An SRE (Site Reliability Engineering) seat is a separate hire, open to you like any candidate. Level 2 incident ownership in the Network and Edge lane Take the network incident the runbook cannot close and own it to root cause. Provide Level 2 escalation support for cloud network incidents and resolve them within SLA (service level agreement) targets. Troubleshoot switching, routing, firewall and interconnect faults and restore service. Post the first substantive comment within two hours of acknowledgment on every ticket you own. Hand off and hand over only with an evidence comment attached; an escalation to SRE or Network Engineering carries your diagnosis. Compare the failing device against its healthy neighbor before you escalate, and attach the diff. Lead the technical investigation on major or recurring network incidents, and supply the evidence for the post mortem SRE writes. Take part in the on-call rotation and in major incident bridges as the network lead. Monitoring, change and service continuity Keep the network observable, and change it safely. Monitor network performance and availability; find and act on degradations before customers do. Execute and validate approved network changes under the change management process, with a tested rollback. Support hybrid cloud connectivity, backbone services, carrier circuits and customer interconnections. Work with Network Engineering, vendors and carriers to resolve escalated faults; own the vendor case until it closes. Automation, runbooks and the record Retire the repeat ticket instead of working it again. Contribute one merged, reviewed automation per quarter in IREN GitLab, with tests: port compares, config diffs, event-burst detection, ticket enrichment. Raise the problem record within a day when a pattern repeats, and execute the fixes SRE designs for it. Maintain accurate runbooks, operational documentation and incident records; author or validate one L1 runbook per quarter. Keep ticket fields (category, vendor, component) accurate so we can measure the fleet. AI-native practice Use the assistant for every draft, and verify every identifier before it posts. Confirm, correct or escalate every triage-agent suggestion in Jira; the logged response rate on eligible tickets is a core KPI, target 80%. Verify every identifier in an assistant-drafted update against a check you ran; report a failed query as “not found”. Build with Claude Code under our engineering rules: code in IREN GitLab, tests before merge, secret scanning on, no credentials in prompts. Name what the assistant got wrong in the monthly lab, and feed the correction back. Mentoring and coverage Lift L1, and keep eyes on glass. Give technical guidance to the L1 engineers and DC (data center) technicians; take one shadow shift per quarter with an L1 engineer. Deliver the shift handover as a written card: open incidents, pending changes and watch items. Job Benefits At IREN, we offer a comprehensive, market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect our commitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performance and long-term growth. Compensation Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications. Relocation and Living-out-allowance (as applicable and based on successful candidate circumstances) Health & Wellness 100% company paid health insurance premiums (medical, dental, and vision) for employees, 75% company paid coverage for dependents Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance Voluntary life, critical illness, and accident coverage available Health Savings Accounts (HSA) – when combined with the High-Deductible Health Plan Employee Assistance Program and wellness resources Retirement & Financial Wealth 401(k) retirement plan with company match Paid professional development and access to financial planning and legal services Time Off & Leave Programs Paid Time Off (PTO) and paid holidays Growth & Development Professional development to support certifications, continuing education, or role related training Community & Culture Company events and team-building activities We value diverse perspectives and believe that skills can be developed. If you’re passionate about this role, we want to hear from you — whether you meet every criteria or not. Your unique experiences might be exactly what we need! IE US Operations Inc., the employing entity and proud member of the IREN group is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We are committed to evaluating qualified applicants and do not discriminate against protected characteristics under applicable legislation. Lead operational reviews, Monthly Service Reviews (MSR), governance forums, service reporting, RAID management, customer escalations, and Service Improvement Plans (SIPs). Cloud & Infrastructure Operations: Govern operational support across Microsoft Azure/AWS, Windows/Linux, VMware, Active Directory, storage, backup, network, IAM, middleware and supporting infrastructure . Ensure availability, performance, capacity, patching, backup, DR, configuration, and operational resilience. Cloud Operations & FinOps: Oversee cloud monitoring, availability, backup, patching, capacity and security remediation. Drive rightsizing, resource optimization, tagging, reserved capacity/savings plans and cloud cost governance using FinOps principles. Lead P1/P2 incidents, executive/customer communication, service restoration, RCA reviews, corrective actions, and elimination of recurring failures. Improve event correlation, alert rationalization, proactive detection, self-healing, AIOps and SRE practices to reduce operational toil and MTTR. Maintain a measurable improvement roadmap covering automation, self-healing, shift-left, incident prevention, service quality, productivity, and cost optimization. Security, Risk & Compliance: Ensure operational controls covering vulnerability remediation, patch compliance, privileged access, IAM, backup/restoration, security incidents, configuration compliance and Disaster Recovery. Coordinate remediation with Security, Risk, Compliance and Engineering teams. People, Vendor & Financial Management: Manage distributed technical teams, staffing, skills, productivity, capacity and delivery performance. Govern technology/vendor dependencies and support budgeting, demand forecasting, cloud-cost optimization and managed-services commercial commitments. Customer & Leadership Engagement: Build trusted relationships with customer and senior leadership. Translate technical issues into clear business impact, operational risk, remediation plans and executive-level decisions while maintaining transparent communication during incidents and service challenges. Strong experience managing enterprise Cloud, Infrastructure and Service Desk operations , preferably within a global managed-services environment. Strong knowledge of Azure and/or AWS, Windows/Linux, VMware, Active Directory, networking, storage/backup, ServiceNow/ITSM, observability, automation and infrastructure security . Proven experience managing P1/P2 incidents, customer escalations, operational governance, senior stakeholders, distributed delivery teams, third parties and service improvement programs . Strong understanding of ITIL 4, SRE, AIOps, DevOps, FinOps, Disaster Recovery and operational resilience . Excellent customer management, executive communication, analytical, problem-solving, commercial and leadership skills . Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, IT or equivalent experience. Preferred certifications: ITIL 4, Azure Administrator/Solutions Architect, AWS Solutions Architect/SysOps, FinOps Practitioner, PMP/PRINCE2 and/or ServiceNow certification . Success Profile A successful Infrastructure SDM will deliver stable and resilient services, predictable SLA performance, strong customer satisfaction, fewer critical/repeat incidents, improved Service Desk effectiveness, increased automation, optimized cloud costs, stronger security/compliance, and measurable year-on-year operational improvement .

Perform security engineering functions, including application updates and patching, in coordination with Engineering, Security, and IT Operations teams. Proactive reporting: Leveraging data from various sources, generate reports and insights to identify and respond to cybersecurity threats and trends in collaboration with various IT teams.   Advanced Technical Escalation & Engineering Collaboration Escalation Support: Provide escalation support for issues and problems stemming from Sound-managed end points and systems managed for IT Engineering services and device provisioning.
